summary: Fast-paced tech-news short-form style (vertical 9:16). A talking-head creator (dark tee, podcast mic, warm dim room) intercut relentlessly with full-screen visual evidence: logo cards on clean white backgrounds, dark-mode screen recordings with rounded corners, benchmark charts, and cinematic AI-generated B-roll. Frequent split-screen layout with the graphic on the top half and the talking head on the bottom half. Median shot length ~1.3s (23-43 cuts/min) with every silence cut out — the energy never drops. Captions are 1-3 words at a time, heavy bold sans-serif in sentence case (never uppercase), pure white; over light or busy footage they sit in a translucent dark-gray rounded pill (TikTok-style). No colored highlight words. Slow punch-in zooms on logos/graphics while they're on screen. Hard cuts only, with a whoosh sound effect riding most scene changes.

zoom.triggerNotes: Slow continuous punch-in on logo cards, charts, and screen recordings for the whole time they are on screen (Ken Burns style), not snappy jump-zooms. On the talking head, subtle alternation between two crop sizes across jump cuts.

transitions.triggerNotes: Hard cuts only — no dissolves, no dips, no wipes. The whoosh SFX does the transition work, not a visual effect.

notes: Layout system: (1) full-screen talking head; (2) split-screen with graphic top ~55% and talking head bottom ~45% — captions sit at the seam; (3) full-screen graphic takeover (logo on white, chart on white, dark screen recording, AI B-roll) while narration continues underneath. Roughly 50-70% of runtime is covered by graphics/B-roll, not the face. Logo cards: brand logo centered on pure white, entering with a slow zoom. Screen recordings: dark UI, rounded-corner window on near-black background. Caption pill: translucent dark gray (#555555 at ~75% opacity) rounded rectangle, used whenever the background is light or busy; plain white text with thin black stroke on dark simple footage. Captions are small relative to frame (~3% of height), always horizontally centered, roughly 72% down the frame. Never uppercase, never colored. B-roll placement is literal: when a product/company is named, its logo or UI is on screen within a beat. Silences are cut so aggressively that consecutive sentences butt against each other; speech never pauses. Music: none or extremely subtle; the mix is voice + whooshes.
